newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel debt swap at around 160p - paper.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel debt swap at around 160p - paper.

text.p: The refinancing package hammered out between debt-ridden Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel Plc/SA and its creditor banks is believed to involve a 1.5 billion stg debt-for-equity swap at a conversion price of around 160 pence, the Times newspaper said in its Thursday edition.

The newspaper said the agreement, which was announced by Eurotunnel on Wednesday without any detail being given, is worth 4.0 billion stg and may eventually lead to the 225 lenders to the Anglo-French company owning 70 percent or more of it.
The deal involves an immediate debt-for-equity swap giving the banks an initial 49 percent control, the Times added.
It said shares in the company were likely to fall sharply when trading in them resumes next week due to the dilution.
Eurotunnel's shares were suspended on Monday at a closing price of 113.5 pence after negotiations between the parties began to look like bearing fruit over the weekend.

The Times said the refinancing package, which aims to solve the problem of Eurotunnel's 9.0 billion stg debt mountain, could also include a convertible bond at 265 pence, wiping out a further 2.5 billion stg of borrowings and bringing the total outstanding debt to manageable proportions.
